haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors never go through the document service or Postgres. They are stored in Redis and sent over the pub/sub channel pres:{docId}.
haiku-low.q2: The client sends at most one per 60 ms, always the latest position. The server silently drops any cursor arriving less than 50 ms after the last accepted one on that connection, with no error or retry.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor and draws it after that revision is applied. A held cursor keeps one slot per connId, holding the highest seq.
haiku-low.q4: If its revision is at or below appliedRev, its position is transformed to appliedRev. If the history is gone (HistoryGone, older than 500 revisions), the caret is dropped until the sender's next update.
haiku-low.q5: The avatar list is keyed by userId, so one avatar shows. One caret shows, from the connection whose cursor was applied most recently. The avatar leaves only when userGone is true, meaning the user's last connection ended.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, within milliseconds, well under the 2 s limit. After a node dies, about 35 s, under the 45 s limit.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis: a ZSET pres:z:{doc} keyed by connId, plus HASHes pres:i and pres:c. Granularity is per connection. Node heartbeats every 10 s refresh expiry (ZADD, rewritten hashes), and all keys expire after 90 s.
haiku-low.q8: The 5 s SWEEP on other nodes removes entries whose expiry has passed. It publishes conn_left, with userGone true if that was the user's last connection, and nodes relay it to their clients.
haiku-low.q9: An accepted cursor is stored with HSET and published on pres:{doc}. Every subscribed node relays it to its local sockets. On the sender's node, the event goes to its other local sockets, excluding the sender's connId.
haiku-low.q10: The client subscribes first, then reads the snapshot, then applies held events. Events arriving before the snapshot are held per connection and sent after it. Duplicates are harmless because seq and set inserts guard them.
haiku-low.q11: The idle user's cursor is stored in Redis, not streamed, so it is included in the snapshot sent to the joining client.
haiku-low.q12: Ordering uses the sender's seq per connection. A receiver ignores any cursor whose seq is at or below lastSeq for that connId, and otherwise sets lastSeq to the new seq.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never go through the document service or Postgres. They go via gateway nodes and Redis (CURSOR script: HSET plus PUBLISH on pres:{doc}).
sonnet.q2: The client sends at most one per 60 ms, always the latest position (trailing edge). The server drops any cursor arriving less than 50 ms after the last accepted one on that connection, silently, with no error, no Redis write and no publish.
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor and draws it after that revision is applied (op flow: remote_op advances appliedRev, then held carets are released).
sonnet.q4: If rev <= appliedRev, it calls transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev) to map the position forward. If that throws HistoryGone (rev older than the client's last 500 revisions of history), the caret is dropped until the sender's next update.
sonnet.q5: One avatar per user (keyed by userId). Carets are per connection, but the UI shows one caret per user: the connection whose cursor was applied most recently on that client. The avatar is removed only when conn_left arrives with userGone true, meaning the user's last connection went. If one tab leaves, only that connection's caret is dropped and the other tab's caret shows.
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: target under 2 s, typically milliseconds. Node death: about 35 s (last refresh up to 10 s before the crash with 30 s expiry, plus sweep within 5 s), under the 45 s limit.
sonnet.q7: In the existing Redis, per connection (connId) per document: ZSET pres:z:{doc} (liveness, score = expiry), HASH pres:i:{doc} (identity) and HASH pres:c:{doc} (last cursor). Each node's heartbeat refreshes entries every 10 s: ZADD with score now+30s, and rewrites the info and cursor hashes from node memory. EXPIRE 90 s is set on all three keys.
sonnet.q8: The SWEEP script, which every node with local sockets on the doc runs every 5 s, removes entries whose score has expired from the ZSET and both hashes. It publishes conn_left atomically with the removal (userGone true if the user has no other live connId). Subscribed nodes forward it to their local clients, who drop the caret and avatar.
sonnet.q9: The CURSOR script does HSET and PUBLISH on pres:doc. Redis pub/sub delivers it to every subscribed node, including the sender's own node. Each node sends it to all its local sockets of that doc except the sender's own connId. A viewer on the sender's own node gets it the same way, via the Redis publish and not directly. The sender's other tabs on that node also receive it.
sonnet.q10: Subscribe first, then read the state (JOIN script snapshot), then send held events. Node B holds pres:doc events arriving before the snapshot is sent and sends them to the client right after it. Overlap is harmless because seq guards cursors and join is an idempotent set insert.
sonnet.q11: The last cursor of each connection is stored in the Redis HASH pres:c:{doc} and is included in the snapshot. Heartbeats keep it re-written, and the client re-sends its cursor every 10 s if appliedRev moved, which keeps stored carets inside the 500-revision history. So idle users show because their cursor is stored, not streamed.
sonnet.q12: By the sender's per-connection seq. The client keeps lastSeq per connId and ignores any cursor with seq <= lastSeq (out of order or duplicate). A held cursor keeps one slot per connId holding the highest seq. Ordering uses seq, not arrival order or revision. The shown caret is transformed forward each time a revision is applied.
